_comment: Zephyr's own kernel test suites, and how each one currently does on
wasm_node. scripts/check_kernel.py runs them and compares.
The point is that the kernel's evidence stops being one suite taken
once. A suite that does better than recorded is the interesting
direction and should be written down: check_kernel.py --update.
fails           the suite finished and some cases failed
does-not-finish the run ended without a verdict: a trap, a panic, or
note: why, when the cause is understood. An unexplained entry is an

suites.note: test_ms_time_duration: a k_timer with a millisecond duration reports no expiry. Timer resolution under virtual time, not yet diagnosed.
Timer duration and period accuracy. Same area as the common failure and probably the same cause.

DEVICE_API_IS() does not recognise a child class. This is patch 0007's documented approximation, now demonstrated rather than predicted: wasm-ld cannot group a class section with its children's, so the end of the group is the end of the class's own section.

test_tickless_slice: the time slice does not land within one tick of its nominal length. Slicing works -- tests/timeslice proves it -- but its timing is approximate, because a slice ends at the next safepoint rather than on the tick.

Traps on the first case. The thread entries take two parameters and are cast to k_thread_entry_t, which takes three; wasm type-checks indirect calls, so the call traps where every other target tolerates it. Correcting the signatures locally makes all 11 pass. Not a port bug and not fixable in the port.
The same signature mismatch, reached through K_THREAD_DEFINE with an entry declared void f(void) rather than through an explicit cast.
Traps after 13 cases. Not yet diagnosed.
test_time_slicing_preemptible fails, then test_lock_preemptible panics. Not yet diagnosed.
Panics after 14 cases. The heap is otherwise untried on this port.
